findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, exposing the MySQL database directly to the internet rather than restricting access to the private application tier.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the database storage (including any sensitive employee data) is not encrypted at rest.

The database password is sourced from var.password and passed in cleartext as the master password with no secrets manager integration, and combined with publicly_accessible=true this significantly increases exposure risk. The password is also interpolated directly into the instance user_data (see aws_instance.catalog_app_server) where it is stored in cleartext.

The user_data script embeds the database username and password (var.password) directly in plaintext, writing them into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user_data is visible via the instance metadata service and often logged/stored unencrypted, exposing DB credentials to anyone with access to the instance or metadata.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on all resources ("Resource": "*"), violating least privilege. Combined with the fact that this role is attached to an EC2 instance profile, any compromise of the instance grants near-full control over S3, EC2, and RDS in the account.

The database security group allows all outbound traffic (all protocols, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which is overly permissive for a database tier and could facilitate data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
No require_secure_transport or equivalent parameter is set to enforce SSL/TLS connections to the MySQL database, allowing clients (such as the app server) to connect over unencrypted connections.
